title: Correctional Administration
description: Study module for Correctional Administration (10% of the Criminologist Licensure Examination), organized by the topics and competencies of the PRC Table of Specifications.
source: PRB of Criminology Res. No. 02 s. 2024, as amended by Res. No. 06 s. 2025
status: Written with AI assistance from the TOS competencies and the laws they name; for faculty review (content/tos/SOURCES.md).

chapters.title: Institutional Correction
chapters.introduction: Institutional correction is the custody, care and rehabilitation of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) in jails and prisons. This chapter covers the theories of punishment, the agencies that run institutions, the handling of PDLs from admission to release, and crisis management inside institutions.
chapters.content:
## Institutional Correction

### 1.1 Penology, punishment and the rights of PDLs

TOS competency 1.1 (12 items): Discuss the theories and principles of Penology, Punishment, Penalty, Sentencing, and Rehabilitation, including the rights, legal limitations, and conditions set forth by the Constitution, Law, and United Nations Declarations.

- General deterrence warns the public; specific deterrence discourages the offender himself.
- The Indeterminate Sentence Law (Act 4103) sets a minimum and a maximum, allowing parole after the minimum.
- R.A. 9346 (2006) prohibits the death penalty.
- The Constitution bans cruel, degrading or inhuman punishment and subhuman penal facilities (Art. III, Sec. 19).
- UN standards: the Mandela Rules (2015) for all prisoners, the Bangkok Rules for women, the Tokyo Rules for non-custodial measures, the Beijing Rules for juveniles.

### 1.2 Agencies, administration and personnel

TOS competency 1.2 (10 items): Apply the functions, organization, administration, management, operations, planning, decision-making process, training, disciplinary process, and accountability of personnel in the BJMP, Provincial Jail, BUCOR, and other facilities.

- BuCor is headed by a Director General (R.A. 10575); the BJMP by its Chief (R.A. 6975, R.A. 9263).
- PDLs never hold keys; guards do a joint headcount and turnover at every change of shift.
- On reliable escape intelligence, security is tightened and a surprise search (greyhound operation) is held.
- Personnel who smuggle contraband are relieved and charged administratively and criminally.
- Overcrowding is eased by coordinating with courts, paralegal help and timely processing of time allowances.

### 1.3 Admission, custody, movement and release of PDLs

TOS competency 1.3 (10 items): Implement the admission process of persons deprived of liberty, release of persons deprived of liberty, security and safety processes and requirements of PDLs inside the institution, visitation, movement, and escorting procedure, the trial of PDLs, custody, control and disciplinary process of PDLs in the BJMP, Provincial Jail, BUCOR, and other facilities.

- Admission: search, booking (records, photographs, fingerprints), medical examination, orientation and classification.
- Visitors are registered and searched, and the food and items they bring are inspected.
- Escorts follow the authorized route without unauthorized stops; remote court appearances are set up when the court orders them.
- Contraband is seized, recorded and dealt with through a disciplinary hearing (Mandela Rules 39-45).
- A missing PDL at headcount means lockdown, recount and immediate report.
- Children are never held with adults (R.A. 9344).

### 1.4 Crisis and incident management in institutions

TOS competency 1.4 (8 items): Evaluate the principles, management, planning, and decision-making of crises and incidents in the BJMP, Provincial Jail, and BUCOR in case of riot, escape, hostage, contrabands, fire, food poisoning, flood, earthquake, typhoon, and other calamities and incidents.

- After an escape, notify the police and nearby units at once.
- Keep food samples in a food poisoning case to find the cause.
- Recurring contraband is stopped at its entry points: visitors, deliveries and staff.
- Before typhoons and floods, transfer PDLs early to safer facilities and stock food and water.

keyPoints.title: Penology, punishment and the rights of PDLs
keyPoints.note: John Howard pioneered prison reform and Maconochie's mark system was a forerunner of parole; retribution punishes what is deserved while deterrence, incapacitation and rehabilitation look to the future.

keyPoints.title: Agencies, administration and personnel
keyPoints.note: BuCor (DOJ) keeps national prisoners sentenced to more than three years; the BJMP (DILG) runs district, city and municipal jails; provincial jails belong to the provincial governments.

keyPoints.title: Admission, custody, movement and release of PDLs
keyPoints.note: No one is admitted without a valid commitment order, and no one is released without a verified release order; discipline follows notice and a hearing.

keyPoints.title: Crisis and incident management in institutions
keyPoints.note: In a riot, contain the area first; in a hostage incident, contain and negotiate through trained negotiators under the crisis committee; in fire and disasters, move PDLs under guard to pre-set safe areas.

chapters.title: Non-Institutional Correction
chapters.introduction: Non-institutional correction lets offenders serve or finish their sentence in the community under supervision. This chapter covers executive clemency, probation, parole, time allowances and the extinction of criminal liability.
chapters.content:
## Non-Institutional Correction

### 2.1 Executive clemency

TOS competency 2.1 (6 items): Discuss the forms of clemency such as but not limited to: Executive Clemency - Pardon, Absolute and Conditional, Commutation of Sentence, and Reprieve; other relevant remedies granted by the Court; other clemency such as Decriminalizing certain criminal acts, Repealed Penal/ Criminal Laws; and Amnesty. Including the processes and procedures of the grant denial/ disqualifications, process of supervision and monitoring, violation of the condition/s, changes in the condition/s, suspension, revocation, arrest of the grantee, early discharge, and release of grantee.

- A conditional pardon is revoked when its conditions are broken; the grantee may be rearrested and prosecuted under Art. 159.
- Amnesty, with the concurrence of Congress, wipes out the offense.
- Penal laws favorable to the accused apply retroactively, unless he is a habitual criminal (Art. 22).

### 2.2 The probation system

TOS competency 2.2 (10 items): Apply the processes of the Probation System from petition, investigation, grant, denial/disqualification, supervision, monitoring, violation of the condition/s, changes in the condition/s, suspension, revocation, trial, early discharge, and release of the probationer, including the role of the probation officer, probation aids, and the victim/complainant in the probation process.

- Filing for probation waives the right to appeal; under R.A. 10707, if an appeal reduces the sentence to a probationable one, the accused may still apply.
- The probation officer reports within 60 days of the order for a post-sentence investigation.
- Probation lasts up to two years for sentences of one year or less, and up to six years otherwise.
- On violation, the court may order arrest and, after a hearing, revoke probation.
- Final discharge restores civil rights and ends criminal liability for the offense.
- Drug traffickers cannot apply (R.A. 9165, Sec. 24); volunteer probation aides help supervise.

### 2.3 The parole system

TOS competency 2.3 (10 items): Apply the processes of the Parole System from petition/ review/ evaluation of the institution BJMP and BUCOR, investigation, grant of the Board of Pardons and Parole, denial/ disqualifications, the process of supervision and monitoring, violation of the condition/s, changes in the condition/s, suspension, revocation, arrest of the parolee, early discharge, and release of the parolee, including the role of the parole officer, and the victim/complainant in the parole process.

- The ISL does not apply to those sentenced to reclusion perpetua or life imprisonment, habitual delinquents, those who escaped, or terms not exceeding one year (Act 4103, Sec. 2).
- A parolee who violates his conditions may be rearrested and recommitted (Sec. 8).
- Supervision lasts until the maximum term ends, unless the Board grants final release earlier.
- The Board reviews the PDL's carpeta and prison record; a parolee needs approval to change residence.

### 2.4 Time allowances and extinction of criminal liability

TOS competency 2.4 (6 items): Discuss the process and grant of time allowance, qualification/ disqualification/cancellation/ revocation of the grant, and the related provisions of the extinction of criminal liability both total and partial.

- Teaching, studying or mentoring earns another 15 days a month (Art. 97, as amended by R.A. 10592).
- Partial extinction: conditional pardon, commutation and good conduct allowances (Art. 94).
- Total extinction: death, service of sentence, amnesty, absolute pardon and prescription (Art. 89).

### 2.5 Preventive imprisonment, GCTA and loyalty allowances

TOS competency 2.5 (8 items): Explain the relevant provisions of the law on PDLs preventive imprisonment, allowance for good conduct, and special time for loyalty.

- A detainee whose preventive imprisonment equals the maximum penalty is released, though the trial continues (Art. 29).
- Recidivists, habitual delinquents, escapees and persons charged with heinous crimes are excluded from the credit.
- GCTA: years 1-2, 20 days; years 3-5, 23 days; years 6-10, 25 days; year 11 on, 30 days a month.
- Special time allowance for loyalty (Art. 98): one-fifth off for leaving during a calamity and returning within 48 hours after it passes; two-fifths for staying.

keyPoints.title: Executive clemency
keyPoints.note: The Board of Pardons and Parole recommends clemency; a reprieve postpones a sentence, commutation reduces it, and a pardon is allowed only after final conviction.

keyPoints.title: The probation system
keyPoints.note: Apply for probation within the period for appeal; those sentenced to more than six years are disqualified; the probationer reports within 72 hours of the order.

keyPoints.title: The parole system
keyPoints.note: The Board of Pardons and Parole may parole a PDL who has served the minimum of an indeterminate sentence and is fit for release; the PPA supervises parolees.

keyPoints.title: Time allowances and extinction of criminal liability
keyPoints.note: Good conduct time allowance is 20 days a month in the first two years of good conduct; it is granted by the BuCor Director, the BJMP Chief or the warden, and cannot be revoked once granted.

keyPoints.title: Preventive imprisonment, GCTA and loyalty allowances
keyPoints.note: A detainee who agrees in writing to the rules gets full credit for preventive imprisonment, otherwise four-fifths; GCTA rises from 20 to 23, 25 and 30 days a month with years of good conduct.

chapters.title: Therapeutic Modalities
chapters.introduction: Therapeutic modalities help PDLs change their behavior, manage their emotions, think differently and learn skills for life after release. This chapter covers the Therapeutic Community, rehabilitation and human rights programs, and reintegration.
chapters.content:
## Therapeutic Modalities

### 3.1 The components of therapeutic modalities

TOS competency 3.1 (6 items): Discuss developmental aspects of therapeutic modalities: behavioral management or behavioral therapy; emotional and psychological; intellectual and spiritual or cognitive therapy; vocational and survival skills.

- Behavior management uses rewards and sanctions to reinforce good behavior.
- Counseling and groups help PDLs manage feelings such as anger.
- Cognitive therapy targets thinking errors, such as blaming others or minimizing harm.

### 3.2 Rehabilitation and human rights programs

TOS competency 3.2 (10 items): Implement the rehabilitation, reformation, reintegration programs, and promotion of human rights programs among the PDLs across all institutions.

- PDLs get at least one hour of outdoor exercise a day if weather permits (Mandela Rule 23).
- Religious practice of every faith is allowed within security rules (Mandela Rules 65-66).
- Decisions about infants of women PDLs follow the child's best interests (Bangkok Rules).
- PDLs with mental illness are referred for care, not punished for symptoms (R.A. 11036).

### 3.3 Reintegration programs and community policies

TOS competency 3.3 (4 items): Evaluate the re-integration programs (TCMP) of the PDL's of BJMP, Provincial Jails, BuCOR, PPA, and the relevant community policies and laws on former PDL's.

- The Therapeutic Community Modality Program (TCMP) uses peer confrontation and support within a family structure.
- The PPA and LGUs share responsibility for aftercare.
- Stigma and unemployment push former PDLs back toward crime.

keyPoints.title: The components of therapeutic modalities
keyPoints.note: The Therapeutic Community uses the community of PDLs itself as the agent of change, through behavior shaping, emotional and psychological work, intellectual and spiritual growth, and vocational and survival skills.

keyPoints.title: Rehabilitation and human rights programs
keyPoints.note: Programs include ALS education, drug rehabilitation, livelihood, pre-release preparation, religious and family contact, and health care equal to that in the community.

keyPoints.title: Reintegration programs and community policies
keyPoints.note: Reintegration succeeds with family and community support, aftercare and job placement; blanket bans on hiring former PDLs hinder it.
